requirements.assertion: On a subscription-capable transport, eth_subscribe with syncing reaches the registered DownloaderAPI.Syncing callback for the bound source and returns the same session's subscription id.
requirements.unknown: Registry inspection or an extracted method cannot establish transport setup, actual callback execution or source identity at runtime.

requirements.assertion: eth_unsubscribe for a known id closes that server subscription error channel and removes its registry entry; true response is distinct from downstream deferred Unsubscribe completion.
requirements.unknown: Do not require downstream completion before the RPC true response; source handler does not wait for it.

requirements.assertion: Unsupported subscription transport, malformed or unknown subscription names and unknown unsubscribe ids preserve their actual errors and do not count as symptom RED.
requirements.unknown: Error shape/version and concrete transport receipt must be pinned; missing API execution is unknown.

requirements.assertion: In the stated finite live-event-loop schedules, every started call returns after verified downstream acknowledgement; no successful completion may be inferred from rescue.
requirements.unknown: No unconditional timeout guarantee, event-loop shutdown behavior or infinite status-producer fairness contract is established.

requirements.assertion: All concurrent calls on this exact subscription object share one uninstall request and do not return before its Once body completes.
requirements.unknown: Different subscription objects are distinct request populations; shared channel or equal names alone do not prove object identity.

requirements.assertion: The event loop removes the subscribed status channel before closing this request's acknowledgement.
requirements.unknown: A closed acknowledgement generated by an arbitrary fake does not prove real map removal.

requirements.assertion: No Unsubscribe call returns before this object's acknowledgement; after acknowledged deletion no later status-channel use is permitted by the method comment.
requirements.unknown: Observe channel use, not just delivered messages; zero observed messages with incomplete instrumentation is unknown.

requirements.assertion: Normal live subscription notification remains observable before cancellation and normal unsubscribe preserves removal/ack/return order.
requirements.unknown: The extracted producer is not a real syncing-progress source or RPC notifier.

requirements.assertion: A finite status offered after uninstall registration but before acknowledgement can be drained without premature return.
requirements.unknown: An infinite competing stream cannot justify deterministic fairness or immediate registration/ack selection.

requirements.assertion: When the same event loop is blocked on this exact sole receiver's unbuffered status, a candidate can drain while offering uninstall and then await acknowledgement.
requirements.unknown: Only an actual callback/close trace can establish the production overlap; the conditional wait graph alone does not.

requirements.assertion: Observe before rescue, then release only owned gates and join all owned goroutines, timers, transports and processes; cleanup error is retained separately.
requirements.unknown: No permission to stop pre-existing or external nodes; fixture cancellation is not production loop shutdown support.

requirements.assertion: Bind original commit/full file, candidate full-file overlay and exact method diff, driver, requirements and public prompt hashes; prove actual tier and normal/mutant results for those bytes.
requirements.unknown: A method SHA or candidate name is not an applied commit/tree, actual binary or final agent HEAD receipt.

preconditions: event loop removes and acknowledges uninstall
same event loop blocked on unbuffered status
ack held then released by owner
two calls same exact subscription object

candidates.rationale: Unbuffered uninstall send precedes draining, so the proved two-sender wait cycle remains in the blocked-delivery conditional schedule; other four finite scenarios can satisfy the stated method predicates.

Outer select offers uninstall while draining. Once it sends, the nested loop no longer offers another request, drains finite late statuses and returns on acknowledgement. Conditional method fit is not full API/fairness or independent acceptance.

Single select offers request and status receive together, then disables the send channel with nil after its first successful send. It continues draining and waits for acknowledgement. The live-loop finite schedule assumptions remain explicit.
Identical bytes to ORIGINAL, same blocked-delivery failure mechanism. A mutation control alias, not a new source defect or independent candidate.
Empty Once body returns without request/removal/acknowledgement. Return speed alone cannot satisfy the handshake contract in any of the five schedules.

nodes: eventLoop synchronous send to sole status receiver
eventLoop receive uninstall then delete and acknowledge
edges: without draining, sole receiver exit leaves status send waiting while uninstall needs eventLoop
deletion precedes acknowledgement; acknowledgement precedes call return
secondary_derivation.candidate_question: Does the candidate add a status receive reachable before uninstall succeeds, without removing the acknowledgement dependency?
secondary_derivation.shared_bias: Same AI author and source hypothesis; different representation is not an independently derived executable oracle.
